headline: GOLD HOLDS AT $4,070, SILVER FLAT AT $52 AS U.S. JOBS BEAT LIFTS DOLLAR — MIDTERM FISCAL TRADE TESTED
snippet: Gold spot held near $4,070/oz and silver steadied around $52/oz on November 8 as stronger-than-expected U.S. October jobs data reinforced dollar strength, testing the fiscal fear trade that pushed precious metals higher after the Democratic midterm sweep. The gold price closed the week approximately flat — confirming support above $4,000 but finding no fresh upside catalyst in macro data that validated Federal Reserve patience. For junior mining investors, the price context remains constructive: the gold-silver ratio at 78:1 is historically elevated, suggesting silver remains cheap relative to gold and could outperform in a renewed precious metals move. The mid-November interim review by Metals Focus and the Silver Institute is the next data point markets will watch for confirmation of the structural deficit thesis underpinning silver's long-term case.

headline: BARRICK MINING REPORTS Q3 TOMORROW — $4,263/OZ GOLD REALIZED EXPECTED, NORTH AMERICAN GOLD IPO TIMELINE WATCHED
snippet: Barrick Mining Corporation (NYSE: GOLD / TSX: ABX) reports Q3 2026 results on November 9, and the release is shaping up as the most closely-watched earnings event in the gold mining sector this week. Analyst consensus expects approximately 818,000 ounces of gold production, a realized price near $4,263/oz and revenues of roughly $5.1–5.3 billion — implying a 22% increase year-over-year. Investors will focus on three questions: whether Barrick's second-half production ramp is on track (management has consistently guided toward H2-weighted output), whether EBITDA margins are recovering above 61%, and whether the North American gold spinoff remains on schedule for a year-end 2026 IPO. Barrick has beaten consensus EPS estimates in each of the past four quarters at an average of 14.4%, but shares fell 8.4% after Q2 results despite meeting operational guidance — suggesting investors want guidance lifts, not just guidance met. Kinross and Alamos also report this week.

headline: BUNKER HILL + SILVER47 CLOSE MERGER — "MADE IN AMERICA" SILVER PLATFORM LAUNCHES WITH $326M MARKET CAP ON TSX
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining (TSX: BNKR) completed its acquisition of all Silver47 shares on November 6 through a court-approved British Columbia plan of arrangement, creating a U.S. silver and critical minerals platform with a pro-forma market capitalization of approximately $326 million. The combined entity — renaming itself Bunker Hill Silver Corp. while remaining listed on the TSX — combines Bunker Hill's Idaho silver-zinc mine, targeting commercial production in Q4 2026, with Silver47's three exploration-stage assets: Red Mountain (Alaska), Hughes (Nevada), and Mogollon (New Mexico). Silver47 shareholders received 0.1724 of a Bunker Hill share for each Silver47 share held, with Bunker Hill shareholders expected to own approximately 57% of the combined company. The deal positions the merged platform to benefit from domestic U.S. silver sourcing incentives as geopolitical pressure on critical mineral supply chains continues to build post-midterms.

headline: INDONESIA CRACKS DOWN ON NICKEL TRADER ARIF KURNIAWAN — LME NICKEL SURGES 2.2% TO $16,125/T, COPPER FALLS TO 3-MONTH LOW
snippet: Nickel prices surged on November 5 after Indonesian authorities announced enforcement action against Arif Kurniawan, a former Glencore trader whose firms are alleged to have operated illegally in forest areas through irregular mining governance, licensing and permitting processes. Kurniawan is reported to have controlled a large share of Indonesia's nickel ore trade — a country that accounts for more than 50% of global nickel production. LME three-month nickel closed up 2.2% to $16,125 per metric ton, with its intraday high of $16,255 the highest level since October 22. Shanghai futures surged 5.3% to 122,550 yuan ($18,375) per ton, their biggest single-day gain since January. The move coincided with copper falling to a three-month low as technology stocks came under renewed pressure. For TSX-V nickel juniors, the Indonesian enforcement risk adds to the structural supply tightness flagged all year amid rising production costs and tighter ore quotas.

headline: PHYSICAL COPPER DEMAND SURGES: YANGSHAN PREMIUM HITS RECORD $217.50/T — CHINA IMPORT APPETITE DEFIES PAPER MARKET SELLOFF
snippet: The Yangshan copper premium — the premium paid by Chinese traders for imported refined copper above the LME benchmark, the most reliable real-time gauge of physical demand in the world's largest copper market — reached a record $217.50 per tonne this week. The record premium came even as LME three-month copper fell to its lowest level in three months, driven by technology sector weakness and macro de-risking. The divergence between paper market and physical market is striking: Chinese buyers are paying record premiums to secure physical copper at the same time macro traders are selling copper futures on demand concerns. For junior copper developers on the TSX-V and ASX, the physical demand signal deserves more attention than the LME price headline. The Yangshan premium has historically been a leading indicator of copper price direction, and a record level sustained at current prices suggests physical tightness will eventually force a re-rating regardless of near-term macro sentiment.

headline: KITCO: WHY THE SILVER PRICE CASE NOW RESTS ON INVESTORS — 46.3M OZ DEFICIT AND COUNTING BUT MONEY HAS NOT RETURNED
snippet: In a November 5 Kitco opinion piece, analyst Przemyslaw Radomski argued that the silver price case after the October selloff rests entirely on the return of investor flows — industrial fundamentals and mine supply data are not sufficient. The Silver Institute and Metals Focus project a 46.3 million ounce structural deficit for 2026, yet silver has underperformed both gold and industrial metals throughout the year. Radomski's key point: a 2027 supply surplus is now being projected by major forecasters, yet they simultaneously expect the average silver price to rise year-over-year — which is only consistent if investment demand bridges the gap. The mid-November Silver Institute interim review, expected within two weeks, will update the deficit figure and investor sentiment data. The analysis highlights the asymmetry: the structural case is well-established, but only new investor buying — not existing industrial demand — will realize it. Spot silver was near $52/oz as of November 8.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER ALERT: CAN THE POST-MIDTERM REBOUND SURVIVE ANOTHER DIP AS DOLLAR TESTS PRECIOUS METALS?
snippet: Kitco's November 6 gold and silver alert asks whether the post-midterm rebound — which pushed gold to $4,050+ and silver to $52 on the fiscal fear trade — can survive a second wave of selling pressure now that the jobs data and dollar have provided a macro counterargument. The analysis frames the current juncture as a tension between the structural inflation/deficit thesis (which argues for precious metals regardless of short-term dollar moves) and the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets when the 10-year Treasury remains near 5%. With the November FOMC meeting on the horizon and Barrick earnings due November 9, the week ahead is data-heavy for the sector. For junior mining investors, the near-term question is whether gold producer equities can sustain the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) outperformance seen last week — the kind of divergence gold bulls argue precedes a broader precious metals re-rating.

headline: RADISSON MINING: HIGH-GRADE GOLD EXTENDS AT HISTORIC O'BRIEN MINE, QUÉBEC — 83% DRILL HIT RATE CONFIRMS DEPTH
snippet: Radisson Mining (TSX-V: RDS) reported a new batch of nine drill holes at its O'Brien Gold Project in the Pontiac region of Quebec, extending high-grade gold mineralization both beneath and adjacent to the historic O'Brien mine and achieving an 83% drill hit rate across all holes reported since late 2024. O'Brien is a historic high-grade gold producer in the Abitibi greenstone belt, and Radisson has been systematically expanding the resource through definition drilling aimed at converting inferred to indicated categories. For TSX-V gold junior investors, Radisson represents a disciplined exploration standard: high-grade, tight drill spacing, continuity confirmed, in a jurisdiction with low permitting risk and established infrastructure. The O'Brien project benefits from proximity to Agnico Eagle's Canadian Malartic mine and the established Quebec mining services ecosystem, reducing future development cost assumptions at a time when gold at $4,070/oz makes the economics of a future mine increasingly compelling.

headline: SUNSHINE SILVER COMPLETES 50,000-METRE INFILL DRILL IN IDAHO — NY BOY VEIN GRADES 7,069 G/T AG OVER 1.0M
snippet: Sunshine Silver Mining & Refining Corporation (NYSE: SSMR) completed a 50,000-metre infill drilling program at its Sunshine Mine in the Coeur d'Alene district of Idaho, reporting multiple vein intercepts exceeding 1,000 grams per tonne silver. The standout result was 7,069 g/t silver over 1.00 metre in the NY Boy Vein — typical of the district's bonanza-grade silver veins, which are narrow but extraordinarily high-grade. The 50,000-metre infill program is designed to upgrade existing resources from inferred to indicated, a critical step toward an updated feasibility study at a mine that produced over 350 million ounces of silver during its operating life. The Coeur d'Alene district is one of the richest silver mining districts in world history, and the current operator is demonstrating sufficient resource confidence to support a financing decision. At spot silver near $52/oz and with Idaho's established mining regulatory framework, the drill program results are a positive signal for the restart thesis.

headline: AMERICAS GOLD AND SILVER HITS CAREER-BEST COSALÁ DRILL RESULTS: 654.7 G/T AG, 1.5% CU OVER 20.5M IN MEXICO
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver (TSX: USA) announced the best grade-width intercepts drilled to date at its producing Cosalá Operations complex in Sinaloa, Mexico, with key intercepts including 654.7 g/t silver and 1.5% copper over 20.5 metres, and 409.3 g/t silver and 0.8% copper over 14.1 metres. Americas G&S is an established silver-copper producer rather than a pure junior — it maintains commercial production at Cosalá while exploration drilling tests extensions — but career-best resource expansion results are significant at a time when mid-tier silver producers are showing renewed market interest. The high-grade copper-silver system at depth offers potential to materially extend mine life at the Cosalá complex, one of Mexico's historic primary silver producers. For investors following the silver producer catch-up trade at $52/oz spot, Americas G&S represents a mid-tier with both near-term production and exploration upside in a single asset.

headline: FIVE CANADIAN GOLD MINERS TO WATCH AS BARRICK EARNINGS OPEN SEASON — VALUATION GAP AT $4,000+ GOLD NEAR HISTORIC EXTREME
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's November 2026 analysis names five Canadian gold miners worth watching as Q3 earnings season kicks off with Barrick Mining on November 9. The analysis focuses on the persistent gap between gold at $4,000-plus and producer equity valuations — a disconnect that has characterized the sector for most of 2026 — and argues that Q3 results are the first genuine test of whether cost management and production reliability can convert record metal prices into the EPS growth the market has been waiting for. Key watch items include Kinross's recent guidance reduction, Alamos's recovery at Young-Davidson, and whether Barrick's Q3 margins improve above 61% EBITDA. The piece flags BMO Capital Markets' view that the valuation gap between gold and producers is now near a historically extreme level — a signal that implies either an imminent producer re-rating or structural quality concerns the market is correctly pricing in. Self-directed investors are encouraged to check individual earnings releases rather than consensus estimates that have drifted lower over the past three months.

headline: UPSIDE GOLD GRABS 59.7 G/T GOLD IN NEVADA — SAMPLING EXTENDS GOLD-COPPER-SILVER SYSTEM AT VENUS-JUNO CLAIMS
snippet: Upside Gold Corp. (CSE: UG) completed its 2026 field exploration program at the Venus-Juno claims in Nevada, reporting grab samples including 59.7 g/t gold and 13.1 g/t silver from the highest-grade site tested. The company notes that the sampling results support the view that the mineralized system extends well beyond zones currently being drilled, suggesting the target is larger than the initial drill programme defined. Venus-Juno is a newly-acquired claim block adjacent to Upside's main project area in Nevada, a jurisdiction with established gold-silver-copper exploration infrastructure and streamlined permitting timelines relative to other Western states. Grab samples are selective by nature and do not represent average grade or continuity — investors should treat the 59.7 g/t figure as a system indicator, not a resource grade. The results will be used to plan a follow-up drill programme, which is when the mineralization claim can be properly tested.
